title: Law and society: the psychology and sociology of the legal system
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Use psychology and sociology to understand legal institutions: courts and juries, policing, eyewitness memory and false confessions, judgment and bias, compliance and legitimacy, access to justice, and how law and society change each other.

weeks.9: Inequality, access to justice and legal aid

blocks.deliverable: Compare formal and informal social control with examples.
Explain three factors that reduce eyewitness accuracy.
Identify the biases at work in a sample deliberation.
Week 7 midterm; explain procedural justice and why it matters for compliance.
Summarize the evidence on access to counsel in civil cases.
Design a study to test the effect of a hypothetical reform.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Research proposal: design a study (invented data allowed) on a question such as lineup procedures or plain-language jury instructions, with a literature summary, methods, expected results and ethical safeguards, in 1,800 words.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
